drivingQuestion: Does using another's domain on Shabbat acquire it for carrying, and how does that fit the two-balconies mishna?
outcomeNote: The dictum is read as 'the law of theft applies'; the mishna is set in a jointly-built partition case.

segments.he: וְרַב לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דַּאֲמַר רַב: אֵין אָדָם אוֹסֵר עַל חֲבֵירוֹ דֶּרֶךְ אֲוִיר.
segments.en: «And Rav» follows «his» regular line of «argument» here, «as Rav said: One person does not impose restrictions upon another person by way of the air.» Since the lower balcony is far from the higher one, it does not prohibit it, although it can make use of it by means of the vacant airspace between them, albeit with difficulty.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא, וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: יֵשׁ גָּזֵל בְּשַׁבָּת. וְחוּרְבָּה מַחֲזִיר לַבְּעָלִים.
segments.en: «Rabba said» that «Rabbi Ḥiyya said, and Rav Yosef said» that «Rabbi Oshaya said:» The halakha of «stealing applies to Shabbat» domains, «and a ruin must be returned to its owner.»

segments.he: הָא גוּפָא קַשְׁיָא: אָמְרַתְּ ״יֵשׁ גָּזֵל בְּשַׁבָּת״ — אַלְמָא קָנְיָא, ״וְחוּרְבָּה מַחֲזִיר לִבְעָלִים״ — אַלְמָא לָא קָנְיָא!
segments.en: The Gemara registers surprise: «This» ruling «itself is difficult,» i.e., it is self-contradictory. «You» first «said» that the halakha of «stealing applies to Shabbat» domains, which at this point is understood by the Gemara as referring to the following case: A person’s house adjoins the ruin of another, and he observes that the ruin has been left deserted by its owner. If this person uses the ruin during the week, on Shabbat he may treat it as though it were his own, by carrying objects from his own house into the ruin and vice versa. «From here» we can infer that a stolen place «is acquired» for the purpose of Shabbat domains, although it does not belong to the person for other purposes. However, you subsequently said that «a ruin must be returned to its owner,» and «from here» we can infer that a ruin «is not acquired» for the purpose of Shabbat domains by the person who used it during the week, and therefore he may not carry objects from his own house into the ruin.

segments.he: הָכִי קָאָמַר: יֵשׁ דִּין גָּזֵל בְּשַׁבָּת, כֵּיצַד — דְּחוּרְבָּה מַחֲזִיר לַבְּעָלִים.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: We should not understand this statement as suggested above, but rather «this is» what Rabbi Ḥiyya and Rabbi Oshaya «are saying: The halakha of» returning «stolen» property «applies to Shabbat» domains. «How so?» This means «that a ruin must be returned to its owner.» In other words, one who uses a ruin during the week does not acquire it even for the purpose of Shabbat domains.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבָּה, וּמוֹתְבִינַן אַשְּׁמַעְתִּין: וְכֵן שְׁתֵּי גְזוּזְטְרָאוֹת זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ וְכוּ׳. וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ יֵשׁ דִּין גָּזֵל בְּשַׁבָּת, אַמַּאי אֲסוּרוֹת?
segments.en: «Rabba said: And we» ourselves «raised an objection» against «our» own «teaching,» as we learned in the mishna. «And likewise,» if there are «two balconies, one above the other,» they prohibit one another. «But if you say» that «the halakha» against «stealing applies on Shabbat,» which means one may not use the domain of another, and he acquires no rights to it if he does so, «why» are the two balconies «prohibited» from using it. The lower one has no right to make use of the upper one.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן, כְּגוֹן שֶׁעָשׂוּ מְחִיצָה בְּשׁוּתָּפוּת.
segments.en: «Rav Sheshet said: We are dealing here with» a situation «where, for example,» the residents of the upper balcony and the residents of the lower balcony «jointly erected a partition» for the upper balcony. Consequently, the residents of the lower balcony share the right to use it with the residents of the upper one.

segments.he: אִי הָכִי, כִּי עָשׂוּ לַתַּחְתּוֹנָה נָמֵי!
segments.en: The Gemara raises a difficulty: «If so,» in a case «where they erected» a separate partition «for the lower» balcony, the residents of the upper balcony should «likewise» be prohibited to use it. As the residents of the lower one are partners in the upper one, they should prohibit its residents from using it.

segments.he: כֵּיוָן דְּעָשׂוּ לַתַּחְתּוֹנָה — גַּלּוֹיֵי גַּלִּי דַּעְתַּהּ דַּאֲנָא בַּהֲדָךְ לָא נִיחָא לִי.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «Since they erected» a separate partition «for the lower» balcony, «they» each thereby «revealed their intention» to the residents of the upper balcony «that: It is not my wish to be» partners «with you.» Consequently, they no longer prohibit the residents of the upper balcony from using it.
